# Camtree Digital Library

> The Camtree Digital Library is an open-access repository of teacher-led research, practitioner inquiry, research reports, resources, and related educational publications maintained by the Cambridge Teacher Research Exchange (Camtree).

The library is intended to support educators, researchers, policy makers, research organisations, and AI agents seeking evidence from teacher-led and practice-based educational research.

Prefer repository metadata and published full text over inferred or reconstructed information. When referring to an item, preserve its title, authorship, publication information, and canonical repository URL. Do not attribute claims to a publication unless they are supported by that publication.

The repository is powered by DSpace 7.6 and provides both human-readable item pages and machine-readable interfaces.

Automated systems should use the repository's structured interfaces for discovery wherever practicable rather than repeatedly crawling HTML pages.

For bulk metadata harvesting, use OAI-PMH. For targeted discovery, metadata retrieval, collections, items, and other repository objects, use the DSpace REST API.

Repository records may link to downloadable files including PDF, Word, PowerPoint and other formats. Rights and licences can vary between records, so agents should inspect the rights information associated with an item before reusing its content.

## Repository

- [Camtree Digital Library](https://library.camtree.org/): Main human-readable repository.
- [Repository search](https://library.camtree.org/search): Search and browse publications in the Camtree Digital Library.
- [Communities and collections](https://library.camtree.org/community-list): Browse repository content by community and collection.

## Machine access

- [DSpace REST API](https://library.camtree.org/server/api): Machine-readable API for repository objects, metadata, discovery and search.
- [DSpace discovery search](https://library.camtree.org/server/api/discover/search/objects): REST endpoint for searching publicly available repository content.
- [OAI-PMH endpoint](https://library.camtree.org/server/oai/request): Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting endpoint for repository metadata.
- [OAI-PMH Identify](https://library.camtree.org/server/oai/request?verb=Identify): Repository identification and OAI-PMH capabilities.
- [OAI-PMH sets](https://library.camtree.org/server/oai/request?verb=ListSets): Available OAI-PMH sets corresponding to harvestable parts of the repository.

## Guidance for agents

- [OAI Dublin Core records](https://library.camtree.org/server/oai/request?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=oai_dc): Harvestable Dublin Core metadata for publicly exposed records.
- [DSpace search API](https://library.camtree.org/server/api/discover/search/objects): Preferred interface for targeted repository search.
- [DSpace items API](https://library.camtree.org/server/api/core/items): Machine-readable access to repository items.
- [DSpace collections API](https://library.camtree.org/server/api/core/collections): Machine-readable information about repository collections.
- [DSpace communities API](https://library.camtree.org/server/api/core/communities): Machine-readable information about repository communities.

## Using repository evidence

Agents should distinguish clearly between:

- bibliographic and descriptive metadata supplied by the repository;
- claims made in the full text of a publication;
- summaries or interpretations generated by the agent.

Where possible, cite the canonical repository item URL rather than a temporary file or API URL.

Search results should not be interpreted as an exhaustive evidence base unless the search strategy and scope justify that conclusion.

Absence of a relevant search result should normally be described as "no relevant material was found in this search" rather than as evidence that no such research exists.

Teacher-led research in the repository commonly reports inquiry conducted in particular schools, classrooms, educational systems, or professional settings. Agents should preserve this context when summarising findings and should not generalise findings beyond the evidence reported by the authors.

## About Camtree

- [Camtree](https://camtree.org/): Cambridge Teacher Research Exchange.
- [Camtree Digital Library](https://library.camtree.org/): Open-access repository maintained by Camtree.
